title: "Declared versus assessed VAT debt by CNAE level, age, status and concentration"
description: "How do size, concentration, payment and recovery differ between declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) debt? December 2025 legal entities, CNAE 2.3, aggregates only."
date: 2026-10-31
jupyter: python3
---

**Data:** December 2025 snapshot of the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract. Payments are GARE amounts dated before 1 January 2026. No 2026 debt and no 2026 payment enter. Firm attributes come from the Receita Federal CNPJ registry already linked to these debtors. Activity uses the official IBGE CNAE-Subclasses 2.3 hierarchy (1,331 subclasses).
**What is shown:** aggregates only. A cell with 1 to 4 firms is left blank in the detailed activity files.
**Status:** exploration. These are the aggregates used by the declared-versus-assessed manuscript. The computation is `analyze.py` in the folder of the same name. This page reads those outputs and redraws the figures.

::: {.callout-warning title="The firm register is later than the debts"}
Registration status, CNAE, size, place and firm age describe the firm as the register stands. They are not measured before the debt. A firm may be closed or unfit because of the debt. Recovery is payments before 1 January 2026 divided by the December 2025 stock. It is not an annual hazard.
:::

## Question

How do size, concentration, payment and recovery differ between declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) debt?

Declared is `ICMS Declarado`: tax the firm reported and did not pay. Assessed is `ICMS Autuação` plus `ICMS Autuação Simples Nacional`: tax fixed by an assessment. Fecoep and the GIA amendment stay out of the comparison.

## Measures

Stock is the December 2025 value net of legal fees. The payment rate is the share of certificates with any GARE payment before 1 January 2026. Recovery is those payments divided by the December 2025 stock. Debt age runs from the enrolment date to 31 December 2025. Dates before 1960 are missing. Firm age runs from the establishment opening date. Dates before 1900 are missing. A firm is the 8-digit CNPJ root. A firm has repeated enrolments when it holds two or more certificates in the segment.

The Lorenz curve orders positive-value certificates from smallest to largest. The Gini coefficient is one minus twice the area under that curve. The top 1 percent is the largest ceil(1 percent of N) positive-value certificates. The Mann-Whitney rank-biserial correlation is positive when a random assessed unit tends to exceed a random declared unit. Cramér's V is the effect size of the chi-square test on firm counts. Except for repeated enrolment, each firm is placed in the segment that holds more of its stock. The samples are large, so every p-value is 0 at floating-point precision. The effect size is the result.

## Size, payment and recovery

Assessed debt is the value. Declared debt is the count. Declared debt is 97.4 percent of the two-segment certificates and 27.2 percent of the two-segment stock. Assessed debt is 72.8 percent of that stock and 2.6 percent of the certificates.

## Concentration and the 1 percent cut

```{python}
#| label: fig-lorenz
#| fig-cap: "Lorenz curves of December 2025 stock, positive certificate values. Certificates are ordered from the smallest value to the largest."
import duckdb
from dotenv import dotenv_values

def repo_root():
    for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]:
        if (p / "pyproject.toml").exists() and (p / "lab").exists():
            return p
    raise RuntimeError("Repository root not found.")

env = dotenv_values(repo_root() / ".env")
interim = Path(env["CEMEPI_INTERIM"])
tmp = Path(env["CNPJ_PIPELINE_WORKDIR"]) / "tmp"
icms = interim / "icms" / "year=2025" / "*.parquet"
if not icms.parent.exists():
    raise RuntimeError("The ICMS extract is not available. Is the external disk mounted?")
con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute(f"SET memory_limit='3GB'; SET threads=4; SET temp_directory='{tmp}'; SET preserve_insertion_order=false")
raw = con.execute(
    "SELECT ICMS_ORIGIN AS segment, VALOR_SEM_HONORARIOS AS stock "
    f"FROM read_parquet('{icms}') "
    "WHERE MES_EXTRACAO = 12 AND ICMS_ORIGIN IN ('declared', 'assessed') AND VALOR_SEM_HONORARIOS > 0"
).df()
con.close()

def curve(values):
    x = np.sort(values.to_numpy())
    c = np.cumsum(x)
    idx = np.unique(np.round(np.linspace(0, len(x) - 1, 201)).astype(int))
    return (idx + 1) / len(x), c[idx] / c[-1]

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[0, 1], y=[0, 1], mode="lines", name="Equality",
                         line=dict(color=GREY, dash="dash", width=1.4)))
for label, mask, color in (
    ("Declared", raw.segment == "declared", DEC),
    ("Assessed", raw.segment == "assessed", ASS),
    ("Both", slice(None), BOTH),
):
    series = raw.stock if isinstance(mask, slice) else raw.loc[mask, "stock"]
    p, ell = curve(series)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=p, y=ell, mode="lines", name=label, line=dict(color=color, width=2.4)))
fig.add_vline(x=0.99, line_color="#C9CED1", line_width=1)
fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    font=dict(family="Arial", size=13, color="#1c1c1c"),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2, x=0),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=10, b=60),
    height=480, paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
)
fig.update_xaxes(title="Share of certificates, from smallest value to largest", range=[0, 1], tickformat=".0%")
fig.update_yaxes(title="Share of stock", range=[0, 1], tickformat=".0%")
show(fig)
```

The pooled Gini coefficient is 0.946. Inside declared debt it is 0.839. Inside assessed debt it is 0.863.

**Source.** December 2025 snapshot of the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract (`VALOR_SEM_HONORARIOS`), declared and assessed segments; CNAE section of the debtor establishment from the March 2026 Federal Revenue (RFB) register, CNAE 2.3 structure, establishment-level matches only. **Representation.** One row per segment × section (manufacturing, trade, transport, information); unit is the certificate (CDA) with positive stock; the Gini coefficient and the share of the section's stock held by its largest 1 percent of certificates are computed inside each segment and section; values, not counts. **How to read.** A higher Gini or top-1 percent share means the section's stock sits in fewer certificates; compare the two segments within a section, not sections with the pooled figure.

```{python}

#| label: tbl-age
#| tbl-cap: "Share of segment stock by age band."
def age_table(frame, order, kind):
    out = frame[frame.band.isin(order)].copy()
    out["kind"] = kind
    out["share (%)"] = out.share_stock.map(lambda v: pct(v))
    return out[["kind", "segment", "band", "share (%)"]]
display(pd.concat([age_table(age, order_d, "Debt age"), age_table(firm_age, order_f, "Firm age")], ignore_index=True))
print(
    "Stock older than 10 years: 39.5 percent declared and 43.7 percent assessed. "
    "Firms aged 20 years or more hold 66.3 percent of declared stock and 76.0 percent of assessed stock."
)
```

## Activity

**Source.** As above: December 2025 stock, GARE payments dated before 1 January 2026, CNAE section of the establishment (RFB, March 2026; CNAE 2.3). **Representation.** Shares of each segment's total stock by section (value), plus the share of certificates with any payment (count) and recovery = paid ÷ stock (value), in percent; sections shown have at least 1 percent of either segment's stock, the rest is pooled in "All other sections"; rows with 1 to 4 firms are suppressed. **How to read.** Read down a column to see where a segment's stock sits; compare the declared and assessed columns of a row to see whether a section is weighted towards one origin; payment and recovery are not stock shares.

```{python}
#| label: fig-section
#| fig-cap: "Share of segment stock by CNAE section."
total = sec.groupby("code").stock.sum().sort_values()
codes = [c for c in total.index if c != "unmatched"]
fig = go.Figure()
for segment, color, name in (("declared", DEC, "Declared"), ("assessed", ASS, "Assessed")):
    part = sec[sec.segment == segment].set_index("code").reindex(codes)
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        y=[EN.get(c, c) for c in codes], x=part.share_stock, orientation="h",
        name=name, marker_color=color,
    ))
fig.update_layout(template="plotly_white", barmode="group", height=640,
                  legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.02, x=0),
                  margin=dict(l=220, r=20, t=30, b=40))
fig.update_xaxes(title="Share of the segment stock", tickformat=".0%")
show(fig)
```

**Source.** As above: December 2025 stock, GARE payments dated before 1 January 2026, CNAE section of the establishment (RFB, March 2026; CNAE 2.3). **Representation.** Shares of each segment's total stock by section (value), plus the share of certificates with any payment (count) and recovery = paid ÷ stock (value), in percent; sections shown have at least 1 percent of either segment's stock, the rest is pooled in "All other sections"; rows with 1 to 4 firms are suppressed. **How to read.** Read down a column to see where a segment's stock sits; compare the declared and assessed columns of a row to see whether a section is weighted towards one origin; payment and recovery are not stock shares.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-section
#| tbl-cap: "Main CNAE sections: stock, payment and recovery by segment. Sections with at least 1 percent of either segment's stock."
want = ["C", "G", "H", "J", "N", "M"]
rows = []
for code in want:
    d = sec[(sec.code == code) & (sec.segment == "declared")].iloc[0]
    a = sec[(sec.code == code) & (sec.segment == "assessed")].iloc[0]
    rows.append({
        "Section": EN[code],
        "Declared stock (%)": pct(d.share_stock),
        "Assessed stock (%)": pct(a.share_stock),
        "Declared payment (%)": pct(d.payment_rate),
        "Assessed payment (%)": pct(a.payment_rate),
        "Declared recovery (%)": pct(d.recovery, 2),
        "Assessed recovery (%)": pct(a.recovery, 2),
    })
d_other = 100 - sum(float(r["Declared stock (%)"]) for r in rows)
a_other = 100 - sum(float(r["Assessed stock (%)"]) for r in rows)
rows.append({
    "Section": "All other sections",
    "Declared stock (%)": f"{d_other:.1f}",
    "Assessed stock (%)": f"{a_other:.1f}",
    "Declared payment (%)": "",
    "Assessed payment (%)": "",
    "Declared recovery (%)": "",
    "Assessed recovery (%)": "",
})
display(pd.DataFrame(rows))
print(
    "Trade is 45.4 percent of assessed stock and 27.6 percent of declared stock. "
    "Manufacturing is 34.5 percent and 50.8 percent. "
    "Transport is 4.6 percent and 12.5 percent. "
    "Information is 6.0 percent and 0.8 percent. "
    "All other sections are 3.0 percent of declared stock and 3.8 percent of assessed stock."
)
```

**Source.** December 2025 certificates and GARE payments before 1 January 2026, by CNAE section (RFB, March 2026). **Representation.** Share of certificates with at least one payment (count-based), sections with at least 2 percent of a segment's stock, one bar per segment. **How to read.** A taller bar means more certificates in that section received any payment; it says nothing about how much of the stock was paid.

```{python}
#| label: fig-payment
#| fig-cap: "Share of certificates with any payment, for sections with at least 2 percent of a segment's stock."
keep = sec.groupby("code").share_stock.max()
codes = [c for c in keep[keep >= 0.02].sort_values(ascending=False).index if c != "unmatched"]
short = {"C": "Manufacturing", "G": "Trade", "H": "Transport", "J": "Information", "N": "Admin. support"}
fig = go.Figure()
for segment, color, name in (("declared", DEC, "Declared"), ("assessed", ASS, "Assessed")):
    part = sec[sec.segment == segment].set_index("code").reindex(codes)
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=[short.get(c, EN.get(c, c)) for c in codes], y=part.payment_rate,
                         name=name, marker_color=color))
fig.update_layout(template="plotly_white", barmode="group", height=420,
                  legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2, x=0),
                  margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=10, b=60))
fig.update_yaxes(title="Share of certificates with a payment", tickformat=".0%")
show(fig)
```

**Source.** December 2025 stock and GARE payments before 1 January 2026; CNAE **division** (2 digits) of the debtor establishment from the March 2026 RFB register, CNAE 2.3. **Representation.** Seven selected divisions; stock share of each segment (value) and recovery = paid ÷ stock (value), in percent; English labels are short renderings of the official Portuguese names; the full list of divisions is in `tables/cnae_division.csv`, where rows with 1 to 4 firms are blank. **How to read.** Compare the declared and assessed stock shares of a division to see which origin it weighs on; low recovery with a high stock share marks where the unpaid stock concentrates.

## What this does not show

The register is observed after the debts, so closure and unfitness can be consequences. Certificate-level tests describe the portfolio. Certificates of the same firm are not independent, which is why the firm-level effect sizes are reported beside them. The 1 percent cut describes where the stock sits. It does not show that collecting those certificates would recover the stock. The evidence is a December 2025 cross-section, not a follow-up of each firm.
